restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, Y4 is held in the sub-class of 131,072 values, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are dropped. A frame (six outer words, the member y and its own D2.a1 = g*, all from one fresh 256-bit word) is one outer step. A 32-bit word K(D2.a1), computed by 29 assignments, equals an explicit word H(E1.d1, E1.a2) for every trial (Lemma AK, from GPT Sol's answer AK). Each frame builds the table of the 2^32 values of D2.a1, keeps K* = K(g*), and scans a fixed table of 53 * 2^26 E1 records; a kept record with H = K* is a root, so the search forms exactly the E1-listed trials of the outer step, at most 2^21, and certifies exactly its listed good trials (Lemmas KT, TG, TG1). Heuristic part: over 843,790,834,046,997,321,198 frames, 2^90.516 trials covered, a collision is found with probability at least 0.40 under H1'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 16 registers; every load is one unit wherever its word lies. Allowances in words from GPT Sol's answer AK, not counted by a program: per frame 4,096 for the random word, the 35 frame lines and K*, 512 per value of D2.a1 for the table (2^32 values, built again in every frame), 64 per E1 record scanned (53 * 2^26 records), 8,192 per root (at most 2^21 per frame) for its reconstruction, the tests of Q*, t and rule A and two last-chunk compressions; 2^46 once for the E1 record table. The run halts with failure after 843,790,834,046,997,321,198 frames; every row is charged at its worst case. With the selection procedure in full, O_tot = 2,062,086,750,949,187,461,726,020,049,229,696 operations, T <= O_tot/430 + 2^38, log2 T = 101.91954 (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per frame. The success probability 0.40 (bound 0.40149) holds only under H1': (i) the rate at 5/7 of the model's conditional count, a margin of 1.40 where earlier entries on this track used half (at half the time_log2 would be 102.4342), and (ii) the factorial bound 0.0065 on the good trials of one outer step of 2^21 trials, the dependence premise of the accepted entries; no premise on a group of outer steps is made. Neither part is measured. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance of the same construction (counter 0, flags 11), because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The search of proof.md Section 9 is defined in the text only and has not been implemented; the submitted program contains steps CO and CT, the compression and the rule A test that it uses.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test, the beta* cube and the seven tau values with eps are stored in the program (92 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by GPT Sol 6.1 from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces. preprocessing_log2 70 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 and the E1 record table and is included in time_log2; the per-frame tables are built in the search and charged in time_log2. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, the selection procedure and the search (below 2^39 bytes: the E1 record table and one frame table, 388,694,540,288 bytes), all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an outer step of the counter construction whose seven outer words are independent uniform 32-bit words and whose member y is uniform in the sub-class of 131,072 values, let N_o be the number of its listed good valid trials over all of the cube Q* of beta* = 18b0e098: t != 0, equal last-chunk chaining values (R = 0), rule A, and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*. Assume (i) E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = (5/7) p = 5 * 1033 / (7 * 2^101), about 2^-91.473, where p = 1033 * 2^-101 is the conditional model rate of Lemma S1; and (ii) E[N_o (N_o - 1)] <= 0.0065 E[N_o]. Each frame of the search of proof.md 9.1 is one such outer step, drawn from its own fresh 256-bit word, so the frames are independent; the run's 843,790,834,046,997,321,198 frames give FRAMES * E[N_o] >= 0.515, and Lemma S8 bounds the probability that no frame has N_o > 0 by exp(-0.515 * (1 - 0.0065 / 2)) < 0.598502. Part (i) is a first-moment statement: it asserts neither independent trials nor independent uniform E1 or E3 words. This is the premise of entry e7b17fd1 and its successors on this track, with the count restricted to the seven outcomes and the factor at 5/7 of the count in place of one half.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t < 2^32, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values, E1.c1 in Q*, t solved per trial and t = 0 dropped, the seven outer words and the member drawn from one fresh 256-bit word per frame. N_o counts all of Q* in the frame's one outer step; the search certifies exactly these trials (Lemma TG1). Nothing is assumed about a group of more than one outer step.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube leaves the E3 side unchanged), taken at 5/7, a margin of 1.40 chosen by the participant; entry e7b17fd1 and the earlier entries on this track took half. (ii) The dependence bound that the entries on this track declare for one outer step of 2^21 trials, unchanged; a frame of this search is exactly one such outer step. Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1% to about 2^-31.7, and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor (5/7) * 138,646,913,024 = 99,033,509,302.86 per 2^128 is assumed; at 5/7 part (i) is stronger than the half-count premise of the earlier entries and is not implied by it (at half the count the same search is priced at time_log2 102.4342). Part (ii) is not proved: Lemma S7 gives only E[N_o (N_o - 1)] <= 3,071 E[N_o], and single outer steps of the counter arrangement differ strongly in partial events (a variance 572 times the mean for rule A). The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision. The transfer of the single-trial law to the construction is partly proved (Lemmas S1 to S4 and IP) and partly assumed here; the share of the success mass carried by the dropped member with t = 0 is not bounded. No measurement of this premise exists at its scale, and the search has not been implemented.
